excerpts: # Pricing and limits
> Understand Model API pricing and rate limits, then track usage and costs
Model APIs bill by token and enforce request and token rate limits for each model. You can set a workspace budget, inspect token usage, and attribute costs by API key, user, model, or service tier.
* [Check your current rate limits](#check-your-current-limits).
* [Confirm account verification or request higher limits](#account-verification-and-higher-limits).
* [Monitor usage](#usage), [inspect costs](#costs), or [set a budget](#budgets).
Model APIs bill per million input and output tokens. Rates vary by model. See the [Model APIs pricing page](https://www.baseten.co/pricing) for current prices.

Baseten serves prompt tokens from the KV cache at a discounted rate when a request reuses a cached prefix. Caching is automatic and requires no request flags. Cached and uncached input tokens count equally toward token rate limits.

Set `BASETEN_API_KEY` to your [API key](https://docs.baseten.co/organization/api-keys.md#use-api-keys-with-endpoints) and install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) to run the example. ## Rate limits
Baseten enforces the following limits for each Model API:
| Limit | Counts |
### Check your current limits

To retrieve the limits for a model in your workspace, set `BASETEN_API_KEY` to your [API key](https://docs.baseten.co/organization/api-keys.md#use-api-keys-with-endpoints), then call [Get a Model API by name](https://docs.baseten.co/reference/management-api/model-apis/gets-a-model-api-by-name.md):
"rate_limits": [

Replace `zai-org%2FGLM-5.3` with your model's URL-encoded slug (`/` becomes `%2F`). Read `threshold` for the `REQUEST` and `TOKEN` entries with `unit: "MINUTE"` to find RPM and TPM. Your returned limits can differ from this example and the account defaults below.
You can also inspect the [rate limit response headers](#rate-limit-response-headers) on inference responses to see your limits and the remaining allowance.
### Default limits by account tier
These are account defaults. A model, service tier, or organization-specific configuration can set different limits. [Check your current limits](#check-your-current-limits) for the model you call.
### Account verification and higher limits

To confirm whether your Basic account is verified and which verification steps apply, [contact support](mailto:support@baseten.co). Include your workspace name, sign-in email, the model slug, and the limits returned by [the model details request](#check-your-current-limits). Keep the full API key out of your message.

To request more capacity for your workload, submit a [rate limit increase request](https://www.baseten.co/talk-to-us/increase-rate-limits/). Include the model, expected requests and tokens per minute, and whether traffic arrives steadily or in bursts. Confirm the effective limits again after your account or model configuration changes.

Changing a request's `max_tokens` controls its output length; it doesn't raise the workspace's TPM limit. Fast variants have separate slugs and rate limits, so [check the limits](#check-your-current-limits) for the exact variant you call.
### Rate limit response headers
| `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` | Maximum requests per minute. |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` | Requests currently available. |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens` | Maximum tokens per minute. |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` | Tokens currently available. |

Rate limits replenish continuously instead of resetting at fixed intervals. Send requests at a steady rate, and use exponential backoff after a [`429 Too Many Requests`](https://docs.baseten.co/inference/errors#429-too-many-requests) response.

A `529 Overloaded` response means that the Model API has no available serving capacity. This response can occur even when your organization remains within its rate limits. See [`529: overloaded`](https://docs.baseten.co/inference/errors#529-overloaded) for retry guidance.
## Budgets

Set a [monthly budget](https://docs.baseten.co/organization/billing.md#monthly-budget) to receive email notifications as workspace spend approaches the configured amount. If you enforce the budget, Baseten rejects Model API requests after the workspace reaches it. Budget enforcement does not affect Dedicated Inference or Training.

For Chat Completions, read request token totals from `usage.prompt_tokens` and `usage.completion_tokens`. The `accepted_prediction_tokens` and `rejected_prediction_tokens` fields in [`completion_tokens_details`](https://docs.baseten.co/reference/inference-api/chat-completions#response-usage-completion-tokens-details) report speculative-decoding statistics. They aren't separate billing counters, so don't add them to completion usage or use them to calculate charges. Rejected predictions can exceed the completion token count.

[`baseten org billing usage`](https://docs.baseten.co/reference/cli/baseten/org-billing) reports total Model API cost as part of the workspace billing summary. The [`GET /v1/billing/model_apis`](https://docs.baseten.co/reference/management-api/billing/gets-model-apis-costs) endpoint returns daily Model API costs and can group them by API key, user, model, or service tier. Both calculate costs from recorded token usage and the model price that applied when each request ran.
baseten org billing usage --jq '.model_apis_usage.total'
scope: Official public Model API documentation; not account-specific entitlement, payment state or confirmed zero-overage enforcement. Documentation GET only, zero inference.
